_about: Common Ontario construction tasks/phases mapped to typical hazards and GENERAL control categories. This is an organizational planning aid to prompt hazard assessment and pre-work discussion; it is NOT a legal compliance document and NOT a substitute for a site-specific hazard assessment. Control categories are kept general and defensible. Anywhere a specific legal threshold, distance, height, weight, or duration would be needed to act, the entry carries a VERIFY note pointing to the authoritative source. Confirm all requirements against the current Occupational Health and Safety Act (OHSA), O. Reg. 213/91 (Construction Projects), and WSIB, and against a competent person / JHSC on site.

_sources.OHSA: Occupational Health and Safety Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. O.1 (Ontario) - general duties of employers, supervisors, workers.
_sources.O_Reg_213_91: O. Reg. 213/91 Construction Projects - the construction-specific regulation under OHSA (fall protection, guardrails, scaffolds, excavation, etc.). Specific thresholds and clause numbers must be read from the current regulation.
_sources.WSIB: Workplace Safety and Insurance Board - coverage, registration, premium reporting, and injury reporting obligations.
_sources.training: Working at Heights (WAH) training is required for certain work using fall protection on construction projects; the approved-training and refresher details must be verified against the Ministry (Ontario) requirements.

_control_hierarchy: Elimination / substitution (design out the hazard, e.g. prefab at ground level)
Engineering controls (guardrails, hole covers, shoring, ventilation, machine guarding)
Administrative controls (safe work procedures, training, signage, scheduling, permits)
Personal protective equipment (PPE) - last line of defence

general_site.label: General site / all phases (baseline hazards present on most construction work)
hazards: Slips, trips, and falls on the level (debris, cords, uneven ground)
Struck-by moving equipment, vehicles, and materials
Weather / temperature (cold stress, heat stress, UV)
controls: Site orientation / new-worker orientation before starting work
Housekeeping program and clear travel paths
Traffic-management / pedestrian separation from equipment
PPE: hard hat, safety footwear, high-visibility apparel, eye protection as required
Hearing protection where noise is significant (VERIFY: exposure limit and when protection is required - OHSA / noise regulation)
MSD controls: mechanical lifting aids, team lifts, training
verify: VERIFY: minimum PPE required by task and current specification/standard (e.g. footwear and eye-protection standards) - OHSA / O. Reg. 213/91
VERIFY: noise exposure limits and required controls - OHSA / Ontario noise regulation
VERIFY: which workers require site-specific orientation and its required content - employer policy / O. Reg. 213/91

framing.label: Wood framing (walls, floors, roof framing)
hazards: Falls from height (open floors, wall/roof work, leading edges)
Falls through floor/roof openings and holes
Cuts / lacerations from saws and sharp material
Manual handling of lumber and panels (MSD)
controls: Fall protection for work at heights (guardrails preferred; travel restraint / fall arrest where guardrails not practicable)
Cover or guard floor and roof openings; label covers
Guardrails at open edges
Tool tethering / exclusion zones below overhead work; hard hats
Saw guarding, sharp-blade discipline, cut-resistant gloves where appropriate
Sequential-trip nail guns and safe nail-gun handling procedures
Eye protection
verify: VERIFY: the height at which fall protection is required on a construction project - O. Reg. 213/91 (do NOT assume a number)
VERIFY: Working at Heights (WAH) training requirement and who must hold it before using fall-arrest systems - Ontario (Ministry) / O. Reg. 213/91
VERIFY: guardrail dimensions and load/strength requirements - O. Reg. 213/91
VERIFY: required capacity/inspection of hole covers - O. Reg. 213/91
VERIFY: fall-arrest anchor strength and maximum free-fall/clearance requirements - O. Reg. 213/91 / manufacturer

roofing.label: Roofing / work on sloped or flat roofs
hazards: Falls from roof edges and through skylights/openings
Slips on sloped or wet/icy surfaces
Struck-by / dropped materials to workers below
Burns / fumes from hot-work or torch-applied membranes (where used)
controls: Fall protection: guardrails, travel restraint, or fall arrest as appropriate to the roof
Guard or cover skylights and openings
Controlled ground zones below the roof; hard hats
Hot-work / fire-watch procedures where torches or open flame are used
Heat-stress management (water, rest, shade)
verify: VERIFY: fall-protection method and trigger height/slope for roof work - O. Reg. 213/91
VERIFY: Working at Heights training requirement - Ontario (Ministry)
VERIFY: hot-work / fire-safety and fire-extinguisher requirements if torch-applied roofing is used - Ontario Fire Code / O. Reg. 213/91

excavation.label: Excavation / trenching
hazards: Contact with buried utilities (gas, electrical, water)
Struck-by excavation equipment; spoil pile hazards
controls: Locate and mark buried utilities before digging (utility locate)
Protective systems: sloping, benching, shoring, or trench boxes as required by soil type and depth
Safe access/egress from the excavation
Keep spoil piles and equipment back from the edge
Barricade / guard the open excavation
Atmospheric testing where a hazardous atmosphere is possible
verify: VERIFY: depth at which a protective system (shoring/sloping/box) is required, and soil-type classifications and allowable slopes - O. Reg. 213/91 (do NOT assume a number)
VERIFY: minimum set-back distance for spoil piles and equipment from the excavation edge - O. Reg. 213/91
VERIFY: utility-locate obligation and process before excavation - Ontario One Call / utility owners
VERIFY: whether the excavation is a confined space and the applicable confined-space program - O. Reg. 632/05 / OHSA

concrete_formwork.label: Concrete work and formwork
hazards: Falls from formwork and elevated pours
Chemical burns / skin and eye irritation from wet concrete
MSD from handling forms and rebar
controls: Formwork/falsework designed and inspected for the intended load before the pour
Fall protection at elevated pours and form edges
PPE: waterproof gloves, eye protection, skin protection against wet concrete
Rebar caps / impalement protection on exposed vertical bar
Controlled zones around concrete pumping
verify: VERIFY: formwork/falsework design, drawing, and inspection requirements (and whether a professional engineer's design is required) - O. Reg. 213/91
VERIFY: rebar impalement-protection requirement - O. Reg. 213/91
VERIFY: fall-protection trigger for elevated pours - O. Reg. 213/91

scaffolding.label: Scaffold erection, use, and dismantling
hazards: Falls from or with the scaffold
controls: Scaffold erected, inspected, and tagged by/under a competent person
Full guardrails and complete decking/platform planks
Stable, level base and proper tie-ins for height
Fall protection during erection/dismantling
Maintain safe clearance from overhead power lines
Toe boards / debris nets to protect workers below
verify: VERIFY: scaffold platform width, guardrail, capacity, and inspection/tagging requirements - O. Reg. 213/91 (do NOT assume dimensions)
VERIFY: minimum approach distance to overhead power lines by voltage - O. Reg. 213/91 / utility (do NOT assume a distance)
VERIFY: competent-person and design requirements for scaffolds above a given height - O. Reg. 213/91

electrical.label: Electrical work / working near energized systems
hazards: Arc flash / arc blast and burns
Contact with overhead or buried power lines
Fire from faults or improper temporary power
controls: Lockout / tagout (de-energize and verify zero energy before work)
Only qualified/licensed persons perform electrical work
Maintain minimum approach distances to energized lines
GFCI / proper grounding on temporary construction power
Arc-flash-rated PPE where an arc-flash hazard exists
verify: VERIFY: lockout/tagout requirements and who may perform electrical work - OHSA / O. Reg. 213/91 / Ontario Electrical Safety Code / ESA
VERIFY: minimum approach distances to energized overhead lines by voltage - O. Reg. 213/91 / utility (do NOT assume a distance)
VERIFY: licensing requirement for electrical workers - Electrical Safety Authority (ESA)

demolition.label: Demolition
hazards: Hazardous materials disturbed (asbestos, lead, silica, mould)
controls: Pre-demolition survey (including designated substances) before work starts
Planned demolition sequence; de-energize/disconnect services first
Dust suppression and respiratory protection as required
Exclusion zones and controlled access
Asbestos/lead abatement by qualified persons where present
verify: VERIFY: designated-substances assessment/survey required before demolition or renovation - OHSA / O. Reg. 490/09 (Designated Substances) / O. Reg. 278/05 (Asbestos)
VERIFY: asbestos work classification (Type 1/2/3) and required procedures - O. Reg. 278/05
VERIFY: silica exposure controls - OHSA / O. Reg. 490/09
VERIFY: notice-of-project / demolition permit obligations - O. Reg. 213/91 / local municipality

material_handling_hoisting.label: Hoisting, cranes, and material handling
hazards: Contact with overhead power lines during lifts
controls: Certified operator and inspected, rated equipment and rigging
Lift planning; rated load charts respected; tag lines to control loads
Keep clear of overhead power lines; spotter/signaller
No one under suspended loads; controlled zones
Daily equipment and rigging inspection
verify: VERIFY: crane/hoist operator certification and equipment inspection/log requirements - O. Reg. 213/91
VERIFY: minimum clearance from overhead power lines during lifts by voltage - O. Reg. 213/91 / utility (do NOT assume a distance)
VERIFY: rigging inspection and rated-capacity marking requirements - O. Reg. 213/91
